pages.note: The whole sheet is one chant, and the book sets it FOUR different ways down the page. Two-column rows finish the บทขัด (verses 4-5). Then a centred heading โอวาทะปาติโมกขาทิปาโฐ — the nominative, where page 72's title has the compound ปาฐะ — which is entered as a section rather than as a new chant. Then justified run-on prose (6-7); then the FIRST gāthā set one pāda to a line and centred, single column (8-11); then the second and third gāthās set two pādas to a line in two columns (12-16); then justified prose again in three indented paragraphs (17-28). Each boundary was measured from the ink, not judged by eye. No footnote, no colophon, no chant number. The passage does not end here — it answers only the lower exposition and the higher one is still to come.

working_notes.invitation: absent, and none written. A continuation carries none by design. What functions as one is verse 5's ภะณามะ เส, 'let us now recite', which is how a บทขัด hands over to the passage it introduces — but it is printed as part of the prefatory verse, so it stays a verse rather than being lifted into the invitation field.
working_notes.units: Twenty-five, verses 4 to 28. Divided at the printed commas and full stops in the prose parts, and one per printed line in the verse parts — which is why verses 8 to 11 are four short lines and 12 to 16 are five longer ones: the book sets the first gāthā one pāda to a line and the other two at two pādas to a line. Grouped into six paragraphs, each marked with para_start and with para_layout saying whether the book runs that group together or sets it as lines.

verses.pali: ตีหิ สิกขาหิ สังขิตตัง ยาสุ พุทธานะ สาสะนัง.
verses.pali_roman: Tīhi sikkhāhi saṅkhittaṃ yāsu buddhāna sāsanaṃ.
verses.english: condensed into the three trainings, in which the teaching of the Buddhas is contained —

verses.pali: ตาสัมปะกาสะกัง ธัมมะปะริยายัง ภะณามะ เส.
verses.english: let us now recite the exposition of the Dhamma that sets them forth.

verses.section: โอวาทะปาติโมกขาทิปาโฐ: The Exhortation Pāṭimokkha Passage
verses.pali: อุททิฏฐัง โข เตนะ ภะคะวะตา ชานะตา ปัสสะตา อะระหะตา สัมมาสัมพุทเธนะ,
verses.pali_roman: Uddiṭṭhaṃ kho tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena,
verses.english: Set forth by that Blessed One, who knows and sees, the worthy one, fully enlightened by himself,

verses.pali: โอวาทะปาติโมกขัง ตีหิ คาถาหิ.
verses.english: was the Exhortation Pāṭimokkha, in three verses.

verses.pali: ขันตี ปะระมัง ตะโป ตีติกขา
verses.english: Patient endurance is the supreme austerity;

verses.pali: นิพพานัง ปะระมัง วะทันติ พุทธา
verses.english: the Buddhas say nibbāna is supreme.

verses.pali: นะ หิ ปัพพะชิโต ปะรูปะฆาตี
verses.english: One gone forth does not strike down another;

verses.pali: สะมะโณ โหติ ปะรัง วิเหฐะยันโต
verses.english: one who harms another is no ascetic.

verses.pali: สัพพะปาปัสสะ อะกะระณัง กุสะลัสสูปะสัมปะทา
verses.english: Not to do any evil, to take up what is skilful,

verses.pali: สะจิตตะปะริโยทะปะนัง เอตัง พุทธานะ สาสะนัง
verses.english: to purify one's own mind — this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

verses.pali: อะนูปะวาโท อะนูปะฆาโต ปาติโมกเข จะ สังวะโร
verses.english: Not to speak against, not to injure, restraint under the Pāṭimokkha,

verses.pali: มัตตัญญุตา จะ ภัตตัส๎มิง ปันตัญจะ สะยะนาสะนัง
verses.english: moderation in eating, and a lodging apart,

verses.pali: อะธิจิตเต จะ อาโยโค เอตัง พุทธานะ สาสะนันติ.
verses.pali_roman: Adhicitte ca āyogo etaṃ buddhāna sāsananti.
verses.english: and devotion to the higher mind — this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

verses.pali: อะเนกะปะริยาเยนะ โข ปะนะ เตนะ ภะคะวะตา ชานะตา ปัสสะตา อะระหะตา สัมมาสัมพุทเธนะ,
verses.pali_roman: Anekapariyāyena kho pana tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena,
verses.english: And in many ways by that Blessed One, who knows and sees, the worthy one, fully enlightened by himself,

verses.pali: สีลัง สัมมะทักขาตัง สะมาธิ สัมมะทักขาโต ปัญญา สัมมะทักขาตา.
verses.pali_roman: Sīlaṃ sammadakkhātaṃ samādhi sammadakkhāto paññā sammadakkhātā.
verses.english: virtue was well proclaimed, concentration was well proclaimed, wisdom was well proclaimed.

verses.pali: กะถัญจะ สีลัง สัมมะทักขาตัง ภะคะวะตา,
verses.english: And how was virtue well proclaimed by the Blessed One?

verses.pali: เหฏฐิเมนะปิ ปะริยาเยนะ สีลัง สัมมะทักขาตัง ภะคะวะตา,
verses.english: By the lower exposition too, virtue was well proclaimed by the Blessed One;

verses.pali: อุปะริเมนะปิ ปะริยาเยนะ สีลัง สัมมะทักขาตัง ภะคะวะตา,
verses.english: and by the higher exposition too, virtue was well proclaimed by the Blessed One,

verses.pali: กะถัญจะ เหฏฐิเมนะ ปะริยาเยนะ สีลัง สัมมะทักขาตัง ภะคะวะตา,
verses.pali_roman: Kathañca heṭṭhimena pariyāyena sīlaṃ sammadakkhātaṃ bhagavatā,
verses.english: And how was virtue well proclaimed by the Blessed One in the lower exposition?

verses.pali: อิธะ อะริยะสาวะโก ปาณาติปาตา ปะฏิวิระโต โหติ.
verses.english: Here a noble disciple abstains from killing living beings.

verses.pali: อะทินนาทานา ปะฏิวิระโต โหติ.
verses.english: He abstains from taking what is not given.

verses.pali: กาเมสุมิจฉาจารา ปะฏิวิระโต โหติ.
verses.english: He abstains from misconduct in sensual pleasures.

verses.pali: มุสาวาทา ปะฏิวิระโต โหติ.
verses.english: He abstains from false speech.

verses.pali: สุราเมระยะมัชชะปะมาทัฏฐานา ปะฏิวิระโต โหตีติ.
verses.english: He abstains from wines, spirits and intoxicants, which are the basis of heedlessness.

verses.pali: เอวัง โข เหฏฐิเมนะ ปะริยาเยนะ สีลัง สัมมะทักขาตัง ภะคะวะตา.
verses.pali_roman: Evaṃ kho heṭṭhimena pariyāyena sīlaṃ sammadakkhātaṃ bhagavatā.
verses.english: Thus was virtue well proclaimed by the Blessed One in the lower exposition.

vocabulary.meaning: patient endurance — bearing what is hard without being moved by it, which the verse calls the highest austerity
forbearance; the capacity to put up with, given here as what khantī consists of

vocabulary.pali: ปะรูปะฆาตี
vocabulary.meaning: one who strikes down another — the verse makes this the disqualification from being one gone forth

vocabulary.pali: สะจิตตะปะริโยทะปะนะ
vocabulary.meaning: the cleansing of one's own mind, the third of the three things the second gāthā names

vocabulary.pali: อะนูปะวาทะ
vocabulary.meaning: not speaking against others; not fault-finding

vocabulary.pali: มัตตัญญุตา
vocabulary.meaning: knowing the right measure, especially in eating
the higher mind — the training in concentration, as distinct from virtue and from wisdom

vocabulary.pali: สัมมะทักขาตะ
vocabulary.meaning: well proclaimed; rightly set forth. The word the prose repeats of virtue, concentration and wisdom in turn

vocabulary.pali: เหฏฐิมะ / อุปะริมะ
vocabulary.meaning: the lower and the higher exposition — two levels at which the same teaching is set out, the lower being the five precepts

checks.issue: A WORD REJOINED ACROSS THE GUTTER. The left cell ends ตาสัมปะกาสะกัง ธัมมะ- with a hyphen and the right cell opens ปะริยายัง, so the row reads ตาสัมปะกาสะกัง ธัมมะปะริยายัง ภะณามะ เส. — the hyphen is typesetting and is dropped. ภะณามะ เส is the standard 'let us now recite', which is what closes a บทขัด, so this is where the prefatory verse ends and the passage proper begins.

THE HEADING HERE IS A SECTION, NOT A NEW CHANT, AND THAT IS A JUDGEMENT WORTH CHECKING. The book prints โอวาทะปาติโมกขาทิปาโฐ centred between the บทขัด and this passage — note ปาโฐ, the nominative, where page 72's title prints ปาฐะ in the compound. Read as the main text of the chant page 72 titled, so it goes in as a `section` on this verse and the two stay ONE chant. The alternative reading is that page 72's title covered only the prefatory verse and this is a separate chant. One look at how the book's สารบัญ lists it would settle it.

THE LAYOUT CHANGES FOUR TIMES ON THIS PAGE, INSIDE ONE CHANT, and it was settled by measuring the ink rather than by eye. Two-column rows for verses 4-5 (gutter at x 940-1100); justified prose for 6-7 and again for 17-28 (no gutter, ink filling the full measure); centred single-column lines for 8-11 (ink only from x 500 to 1140, clear margin both sides); two-column rows again for 12-16 (gutter at x 940-1100). Each prose group carries para_layout 'prose' and each verse group 'lines', so the app sets each part the way the page sets it.

THE FIRST GĀTHĀ IS SET ONE PĀDA TO A LINE AND CENTRED, where the two that follow it are set two pādas to a line in two columns. Same chant, same page, three verses, two settings — so these four lines are four verses and the next five rows are five verses, each verse being one printed line as the book sets it. Measured, not judged: this block has no gutter and clear margins on both sides, and the block below it has a gutter.

NO PUNCTUATION ANYWHERE IN THE FIRST GĀTHĀ. None of the four lines ends with a comma or a stop, where the second and third gāthās close with a full stop at verse 16. Reproduced as printed. The English supplies the sentence breaks the sense needs, which is why its punctuation does not match the Pali's here.

ปาติโมกเข with ต, matching this chant's title and its verse 7, and differing from the ปาฏิโมกขัง with ฏ printed in the chant above it on page 72. The same split runs through both pages. Separately, ปะฏิวิระโต at verses 23 to 27 uses ฏ — but that is paṭivirato, a different word, so it is not part of the same question.

A PARAGRAPH BREAK FALLS MID-SENTENCE. This paragraph ends ภะคะวะตา, with a COMMA, not a full stop, and the next paragraph opens กะถัญจะ. So the book starts a new indented paragraph inside an unfinished sentence. Reproduced exactly as printed rather than closed off — the paragraph breaks are the book's and are recorded with para_start.

A WORD REJOINED ACROSS A LINE BREAK. The line ends สุราเมระยะ- with a hyphen and the next opens มัชชะปะมาทัฏฐานา, so the word is สุราเมระยะมัชชะปะมาทัฏฐานา and the hyphen is dropped. Also note โหตีติ here where verses 23 to 26 all end โหติ — the extra ติ is the quotative closing the list, and it is printed.

THE CHANT DOES NOT END ON THIS PAGE. The last paragraph answers only the FIRST half of the question verse 20 and 21 set up — the lower exposition — and the higher exposition has not been given, so the passage plainly carries on. It is listed in batch_status.continues and carries continues: true.

THE ENGLISH IS A WORKING TRANSLATION AND NEEDS YOUR EYE. The page prints no Thai translation. Verses 8 to 16 are the three gāthās of the Ovāda-pāṭimokkha, among the most quoted verses in the canon, so their English is the most likely to be compared against a version you already know — it was written from what is printed here rather than recalled, and it will not match any particular published translation word for word.
NOTHING ELSE IS ON THIS PAGE. No footnote rule and no footnote, no colophon, no rubric, no chant number. The foot of the sheet below the last line is clear paper.

batch_status.notes: THE LAYOUT CHANGES FOUR TIMES INSIDE ONE CHANT, which is the whole story of this page and the reason it needed the paragraph-level para_layout before it could be entered at all. Chant-level `layout` can only say prose OR lines, and this page is both: prose around the three gāthās, which are set as verse lines — and the first gāthā centred one pāda to a line while the second and third run two pādas to a line in two columns. Every boundary was settled by measuring the ink across the measure rather than by eye, and the measurements are in the check on verse 6. Three other things. (1) THE HEADING โอวาทะปาติโมกขาทิปาโฐ IS ENTERED AS A SECTION, not as a new chant, so the บทขัด and the passage stay one chant under page 72's title. That is a judgement and it carries a check. (2) A PARAGRAPH BREAK FALLS MID-SENTENCE at verse 21, which ends with a comma — the book's own break, reproduced. (3) ปาติโมกเข keeps ต here, consistent with this chant throughout and still differing from the ปาฏิโมกขัง of the chant above it on page 72. Nothing on this page needs re-photographing.
